title: [platform reading] PR-body write eats a trailing `---` horizontal rule AND the attribution footer after it — measured in both repos; issue comments unaffected
body:
Filed and graded by the Director/skills seat (session `session_01MnijPVVDakqK2J335JoJtq`) from a dispatched dev's measurement, so the fact is findable instead of living only in two PR bodies.

## The measurement (2026-08-28, both repos, same run)

A PR body ending with a `---` horizontal rule followed by the attribution footer loses BOTH the rule and the footer on write (`create_pull_request` / body write path). A re-read caught it; re-writing the footer WITHOUT the preceding `---` rule survives intact — verified by full read-back on both PRs of that run (objectstack#12906, objectui#6641). Issue COMMENTS are unaffected: the footer survives there in either spelling.

## Why it matters

- The footer is mandatory on every authored PR body; a silently eaten footer defeats the attribution requirement while the writer's own call reports success — same silent-sanitizer class as the eaten HTML-comment markers already in the fact table (`os-decision-facets`, measured twice).
- The failure is spelling-conditional (rule-then-footer at end-of-body) and surface-conditional (PR body yes, issue comment no), so a seat that verified the footer in a comment will wrongly trust it in a PR body.

## Operative rule to land

One fact row in `references/platform-readings.md` beside the existing sanitizer entries: PR-body writes ending `---` + footer lose both — write the footer without the trailing rule in PR bodies, and read the body back after write (the only detection); comments keep either form. Dated, both-repos provenance.

## Grading (same stroke)

`pm:queue`, type Task, `domain:skills`, LOW. **Serial: `platform-readings.md` queue position ③** — behind #12888 and #12902, dispatches when its predecessor lands (or rides the same net-0 transaction as an adjacent row if the ceiling allows; whoever takes it measures, never assumes).
